criteria.source: Automated `check.py lifecycle` on the real Gateway: pair_calls both tools callable, stop button -> UI 'Gateway 已停止' + unavailable() confirms initialize refused, start button -> 'Gateway 運作中' + both tools callable again, restart button -> same. Manual: cold POST /api/gateway/start 13.7s -> state=running pid=24108 with 'Readiness (/health/ready): ready'; POST /api/gateway/stop -> state=stopped with 3050 released and all 1mcp processes gone. Port-occupied start returns state=error, never Running (see AC-4).
criteria.limitations: Tool calls are proven to traverse the Gateway (fixture gateway_url is http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp; gateway log grew 8958 bytes during a check.py run; manual tools/call against 127.0.0.1:3050/mcp returned 'The sum of 2 and 3 is 5.' and 'The sum of 40 and 2 is 42.'). Downstream-layer health is not part of this criterion: with the http downstream killed, the Gateway still reports running and /health/ready still 200 while the http tool returns -32603. That is T-007 scope, recorded as a known limitation.

criteria.source: Scenario 1, port squatter: an unrelated node process (PID 42288) held 127.0.0.1:3050; POST /api/gateway/start returned HTTP 200 in 36.5s with state=error and message 'startup timed out after 30 seconds: port 3050 may be occupied by another process, or the Gateway is unresponsive'; PID 42288 still alive and still OwningProcess of 3050. Scenario 2, unconfirmable identity: server.pid overwritten with '99999'; GET status returned state=unknown with CLI error 'Runtime PID metadata is malformed; retained for manual recovery'; POST stop returned state=error 'stop command sent, but a running process was detected'; real runtime 44020 stayed alive and 3050 stayed listening. Recovery: after clearing processes and server.pid, start returned state=running in 18.8s and server.pid was regenerated.
criteria.limitations: Cleanup safety verified directly: with server.pid deleted and a squatter (PID 20996) owning 3050, `1mcp --config-dir ... --stop` returned in 1.0s with 'No runtime is running in this Runtime Scope', exit 0, leaving the squatter alive and still owning the port. PID-file corruption was tested by rewriting the file, not by killing the process and letting it go stale; no case where a valid PID file pointed at an unrelated live process was exercised.

criteria.source: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3100 -State Listen shows LocalAddress 127.0.0.1 only; config.js hardcodes hub.host = '127.0.0.1' with a comment stating the admin page is local-only by design and never configurable to 0.0.0.0. From the host: http://100.119.224.46:3100/ and https://alvin.tail63d20f.ts.net:3100/ both refused. From WSL tailnet node alvin-1 (100.79.209.7): http://100.119.224.46:3100/ returned curl 000. `tailscale serve status` and `tailscale funnel status` both list exactly one rule, 'https://alvin.tail63d20f.ts.net (tailnet only) |-- /mcp proxy http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp'; port 3100 never appears in the proxy configuration.
criteria.limitations: The criterion names the iPhone's private remote path and that device was NOT tested; this entry is deliberately left UNVERIFIED and non-critical rather than promoted to PASS on inference. Two independent mechanisms are verified and neither admits a tailnet route to 3100: the listener binds 127.0.0.1 only, and neither `tailscale serve status` nor `tailscale funnel status` contains any rule for 3100 (the sole rule is 'https://alvin.tail63d20f.ts.net (tailnet only) |-- /mcp proxy http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp', tailnet only, no Funnel). A probe from WSL tailnet node alvin-1 (100.79.209.7) to http://100.119.224.46:3100/ returned curl 000. What remains unobserved is the device-side click itself. A delegated reviewer independently flagged the gap; the coordinator agrees and is recording it rather than closing it. OBLIGATION: close this before T-010 by having the operator open the admin URL from the iPhone over Tailscale and record connection-refused, then promote this criterion to PASS with that evidence. Also untested: whether another local user account can reach 127.0.0.1:3100 (recorded as F-04).

criteria.source: A delegated reviewer (collaboration/runs/review-T002-r1, nemotron-3-ultra) raised 6 blocking findings. Two were disproved by direct test: (a) 'pair_calls bypasses the Gateway' is false, Checks.__init__ binds self.gateway to cfg['gateway_url'] = http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp; (b) 'timeout cleanup --stop may kill a foreign process' is false, the CLI no-ops without a valid PID file. Four are recorded as non-blocking F-01..F-04 in .harness/review-notes/T-002.md. None of them changes a T-002 acceptance criterion.
criteria.limitations: The delegated reviewer is a free-tier model and its reasoning was treated as a hypothesis list, not as a verdict; every blocking claim was independently reproduced or refuted by the coordinator.

changes.summary: Process control for the 1mcp agent CLI (--status/--background/--stop). Shells out through an injected run() seam and imposes hard deadlines (start 30s, stop/status 15s) because the real CLI blocks forever with no error and no exit when the target port is already taken - verified against the real binary as a >100s 'runtime starting...' loop with no EADDRINUSE reaching the exit code. parseStatus maps the CLI's observed exit codes (0 running / 3 stopped / 4 starting) and distinguishes ready from transiently-not-ready via the /health/ready line, because the CLI's own 'Servers: X/Y ready' tally printed 0/0 while both configured downstreams were actually serving. start() and stop() both re-query --status after acting and refuse to report running/stopped when the re-query disagrees.

Fastify server on 127.0.0.1:3100 serving public/ plus four admin routes: GET /api/gateway/status, POST /api/gateway/start, POST /api/gateway/stop, POST /api/gateway/restart. Each returns the controller result verbatim. No authentication and no Origin check; see the F-03 note in the review-notes change below.

Resolves the gateway config dir (GATEWAY_CONFIG_DIR, default %USERPROFILE%/.mcp-hub/gateway-config) and creates it with an empty mcp.json on first run, so the single-entry requirement holds before any MCP server has been added. hub.host is hardcoded 127.0.0.1 and is deliberately not configurable, with no environment variable that could widen it.

Spawns the Hub server detached with stdio ignored, unrefs it, then opens the default browser at the admin URL after a fixed 1.5s delay. The delay is not a readiness wait: with an unrelated process holding 3100, the Hub process never started, EADDRINUSE was swallowed by stdio:'ignore', and the browser still opened onto the foreign page. Finding F-01, assigned to T-007.

The single entry point. Changes to the app directory and runs bin/launch.js. Note it does not itself set GATEWAY_CONFIG_DIR: daily use takes the default %USERPROFILE%/.mcp-hub/gateway-config, while the isolated acceptance run must inject the variable from the caller.

Minimal admin page: start/stop/restart buttons and an aria-live status region. The client maps controller states to Chinese labels; the CSS styles running, stopped and error but not unknown, so a status query returning unknown renders in neutral grey. Finding F-02.
Pins @1mcp/agent 0.38.2, fastify 5.12.5, @fastify/static 10.1.5 as exact versions. Scripts: start, test (node --test test/).
16 unit tests over the injected run() seam, covering timeout, already-running/already-stopped short circuits, post-action re-query disagreement, and error propagation.

Full manual test record for this ticket, including every command and observed output. Also carries four non-blocking findings and three items that could NOT be verified in this session and are therefore not claimed as passed. (1) AC-5 from the iPhone: the criterion names the iPhone's private remote path and no iPhone was driven. The mechanism is verified - the listener binds 127.0.0.1 only, neither `tailscale serve status` nor `tailscale funnel status` contains any rule for 3100 (the sole rule is /mcp proxy to 127.0.0.1:3050/mcp, tailnet only, no Funnel), and a probe from WSL tailnet node alvin-1 (100.79.209.7) to http://100.119.224.46:3100/ returned curl 000 - but the device-side click is absent, so AC-5 is recorded UNVERIFIED in the review payload and is an obligation to close before T-010. (2) F-03, admin API exposure: an unauthenticated cross-origin POST /api/gateway/start carrying Origin: https://evil.example.com returned HTTP 200 and actually started the Gateway; same-origin policy blocks reading the body, but a simple cross-origin POST still dispatches, so any web page can stop or restart the Gateway. PLAN-5 and PLAN-6 keep admin authentication outside V1, so this is a documented threat-model limitation. (3) Cross-user local access to 127.0.0.1:3100 was not tested (F-04). (4) Downstream-layer failure isolation: with the http downstream on 3051 killed, the Hub still reported state=running and /health/ready still returned 200 while the http tool returned -32603 'Error calling tool' and the stdio tool still worked. The Gateway's own readiness cannot detect a dead downstream; that is T-007 scope. A delegated reviewer (collaboration/runs/review-T002-r1) independently raised the iPhone gap and flagged this readiness limitation.
